# fastf 3.12.1: reconcile finishes what a cloud mount left

Nothing about an existing project changes. Every `PROJECT_INFO.md`,
`config.toml` and template works untouched, and no command, flag or file format
was removed. A move that 3.12.0 left waiting is finished by the first
`fastf reconcile` you run with this version.

This release comes out of moving a project onto a Google Drive folder mounted
with rclone. 3.12.0 kept the original whole, as designed, but then asked for
three files to be copied by hand. That is not fastf's job to hand over, so:

## Reconcile completes the moved copy itself

When the moved copy turns out to be missing anything the original still holds,
fastf copies it again from the original and checks again: in the move itself
first, and on every reconcile after. The original stays whole until the copy is
complete. Only missing entries are put back; something that is there but
differs (older than what was moved, or another kind of entry) is your decision,
and both copies stay, both listed, until it is made. No message suggests
deleting anything any more.

## No folder on the target is renamed

A cloud mount with a cache uploads in the background, and renaming a folder
while its uploads are still in flight can leave some of them at the old path,
with the mount's own view showing nothing wrong. 3.12.0 renamed its finished
copy into place, which is how the three files went missing. A move now copies
straight into the project's final folder and writes `PROJECT_INFO.md` last, so
the folder becomes a project in one step and there is nothing to misplace. For
a move 3.12.0 left behind, reconcile moves any file the mount put in the old
staging folder back into place, and never deletes one.

The move's own record on the target is written the same way: every file in
it is created once and never renamed, and a phase is a file whose name says
which phase was reached. 3.12.0 rewrote its record by rename for each phase,
and on the same mount the copy on Drive still said "copying" about a move
that had long since finished.

## Each file is written once

3.12.0 created every file empty and then wrote its contents, which on a cloud
mount uploads each file twice, the second write cancelling the first. Files are
now written once. A folder or file name the target will not hold is still found
before anything is published, and a drive that ignores case is asked so up
front, so two names that differ only in case are found before any copying.

## The same word on both surfaces

The app's `!` is now called Reconcile, with "check and recover" as its
description, and the same thing as `fastf reconcile` on the command line. A
message in the app that used to tell you to run `fastf reconcile` now names the
key.

## Also

- A link on an rclone mount without `--links` is refused by name, before
  anything is copied.
- Reconcile no longer claims a hidden leftover is redundant when something in
  it was kept on purpose.
